NON_COMPETE.topic: Post-Termination Non-Compete and Restraint of Profession
landmark_citations: Percept D'Mark (India) Pvt. Ltd. v. Zaheer Khan, (2006) 4 SCC 227
Niranjan Shankar Golikari v. Century Spinning and Mfg. Co., AIR 1967 SC 1098
Superintendence Company of India v. Krishan Murgai, AIR 1980 SC 1717
NON_COMPETE.judicial_consensus_summary: Indian courts consistently hold that restrictive covenants extending beyond the term of employment are void under Section 27. The doctrine of restraint applies strictly; Indian courts do not apply the English 'rule of reasonableness' to post-employment restrictions. A company cannot restrain an employee from joining a competitor post-termination, though it may protect trade secrets.
NON_COMPETE.why_advocate_required: Whether proprietary knowledge constitutes protectable trade secrets versus general employee skill is a complex question of fact requiring formal judicial pleadings.
questions_for_counsel: Does this post-employment restriction violate Section 27 under the Percept D'Mark precedent?
Can the employer seek an ex-parte injunction against my new employment?
Does the geography scope ('anywhere in India') render the restriction overly broad on its face?

LIQUIDATED_DAMAGES.topic: Stipulated Financial Penalties and Early Departure Damages
landmark_citations: Kailash Nath Associates v. Delhi Development Authority, (2015) 4 SCC 136
Fateh Chand v. Balkishan Dass, (1964) 1 SCR 515
ONGC Ltd. v. Saw Pipes Ltd., (2003) 5 SCC 705
LIQUIDATED_DAMAGES.judicial_consensus_summary: Under Section 74, naming a fixed liquidated damages sum does not confer automatic right to that amount. The claimant must prove actual legal injury or quantifiable loss. Liquidated damages are only granted without proof of loss where proof of actual damage is virtually impossible. Courts award only reasonable compensation, not punitive penalties.
LIQUIDATED_DAMAGES.why_advocate_required: Determining whether the stipulated figure is a genuine pre-estimate of loss or an unconscionable in-terrorem penalty requires an advocate to evaluate employer expenditure records.
questions_for_counsel: Is the company required to prove actual replacement or hiring expense before enforcing this penalty?
Can a court reduce the damages amount under Section 74 to nominal compensation?
Can the employer withhold salary or experience certificates to coerce payment of this sum?

EMPLOYMENT_BOND.topic: Employment Minimum Commitment Bonds and Training Cost Forfeiture
landmark_citations: Toshniwal Brothers Pvt. Ltd. v. E.S. Eswaraprashad, (1997) 2 LLJ 222 (Mad)
Sicpa India Ltd. v. Manas Pratim Deb, MANU/DE/4436/2011
Vijaya Minerals Pvt. Ltd. v. Bikash Deb, AIR 1996 Cal 67
EMPLOYMENT_BOND.judicial_consensus_summary: Employment bonds demanding repayment of arbitrary sums are scrutinized severely. Indian courts enforce bonds only to the extent of actual money and resources spent by the employer on specialized external training. Forfeiture of substantial sums without tangible training is deemed unconscionable restraint.
EMPLOYMENT_BOND.why_advocate_required: An advocate must examine whether formal training invoices exist or if normal on-the-job orientation was mislabeled as specialized training.
questions_for_counsel: Has the employer maintained documented proof of specialized training expenses for my role?
Is the 12-month minimum lock-in period enforceable against an at-will employee?
Can the bond amount be challenged as an invalid penalty under Section 74?

TENANCY_DEPOSIT_LOCKIN.topic: Residential Lease Lock-in Period & Security Deposit Deductions
TENANCY_DEPOSIT_LOCKIN.statutory_anchor: Transfer of Property Act, 1882 Section 106 & State Rent Control Jurisprudence
landmark_citations: Kailash Nath Associates v. DDA, (2015) 4 SCC 136
Karnataka Rent Act, 1999 Section 15 & Urban Tenancy Precedents
TENANCY_DEPOSIT_LOCKIN.judicial_consensus_summary: In residential tenancy agreements, landlords have an equitable obligation to mitigate damages by making reasonable efforts to re-let the property. Landlords cannot unilaterally forfeit multi-month security deposits for ordinary wear and tear without itemized invoices and tenant consent.
TENANCY_DEPOSIT_LOCKIN.why_advocate_required: Local civil courts and rent control tribunals have specific local procedures for recovering improperly withheld deposits.
questions_for_counsel: Can the landlord legally withhold deposit for repainting after standard residential usage?
Does the landlord have an enforceable duty to mitigate loss if I find a replacement tenant?
Can I initiate summary recovery proceedings before the jurisdictional Small Causes Court?

UNILATERAL_TERMINATION.topic: Unilateral Immediate Termination and Asymmetric Notice Periods
landmark_citations: Central Inland Water Transport Corp. v. Brojo Nath Ganguly, AIR 1986 SC 1571
Delhi Transport Corporation v. D.T.C. Mazdoor Congress, AIR 1991 SC 101
UNILATERAL_TERMINATION.judicial_consensus_summary: Clauses providing an employer or dominant party unilateral right to terminate at will without assigning reasons while imposing onerous notice obligations on the employee are contrary to public policy and void under Section 23 where unequal bargaining power is demonstrated.
UNILATERAL_TERMINATION.why_advocate_required: Pleading unequal bargaining power and public policy violations under Section 23 requires constitutional and commercial legal counsel.
questions_for_counsel: Is an asymmetric notice period (e.g., 30 days for employer, 90 days for employee) challengeable under Section 23?
Can I claim salary in lieu of notice if terminated immediately without just cause?
Does the termination clause qualify as an unconscionable bargain under the Brojo Nath Ganguly precedent?
